### The checker models a line logged at WARNING as spring-jcl logs it, so example 287's preservation reaches both sides' bcrypt

change `unswkkxpxtvk` · [log `fda3769957a6`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/f28025bc-e46b-4a87-a943-bfb79dea5465/fda3769957a6e5d712f818f60dd7bc1e81d57b724b0cdd8b5e28f6cc89e81ea9.jsonl.gz)

java.util.logging at INFO, WARNING and SEVERE is now modelled under the JDK's default configuration (lib/src/bmc/runtime.rs). isLoggable is true there. A LogRecord's constructor of a level and a message (NullPointerException for a null level) and its setters do nothing a check observes. A Logger's resource bundle and bundle name are null. Logger.log(record) returns normally under a second stated assumption: the record goes only to the root's default ConsoleHandler, and no logger has a filter, handler or bundle. The handler formats the record by calling its getters, which a subclass may override. So log is modelled only for a record whose class below LogRecord writes nothing but its own fields and calls nothing but its own methods, LogRecord's, String's, StackTraceElement's and a Throwable's constructors and getters. A bytecode scan checks this, and spring-jcl's LocationResolvingLogRecord passes. A logging call the model does not take is now the gap it is to a checker without the model; before, an isLoggable the model declined was counted exact. String.valueOf(Object) of a String or null is modelled before the static classification, so the gap scan still names it for other objects.

Countermodels came first, in lib/tests/fixtures/claims/claims/Logged.java. On a JVM each returns false or throws where a model that took logging for granted would say true: a record that counts its formatting, a level, a filter and a handler set on a logger, and valueOf of an object whose toString counts. All five now stop the proof. With the confinement scan disabled, the counting record was falsely verified. The claims test a_line_logged_at_warning_returns_normally_and_what_would_make_logging_observable_stops_the_proof also proves the warned path, the null cases and loud. P.loud moved there, since INFO is now modelled. lib/README.md and 287's notes say what changed.

Probes on example 287's preservation: a trial at bound 8 verifies. At the claim's bound of 80, with a 200 s timeout, the pair reaches both sides' bcrypt and ends on a spurious counterexample past the invariants of BCrypt.crypt_raw and ekskey; a JVM run shows it is no counterexample. This is the relational failure the stream's brief predicts, and step 2 starts from it. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (26 of 26), the lint, and validate_example.py 287.

Item 3 of the challenge brief. Seven lemmas were proved and their summaries made the checker prove properties a JVM contradicts (fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/lemma-countermodels, its README has the table).

The first group is an initializer cycle that calls the lemma's method before the final static field it reads is written (seen and heldSeen: proved 7, a JVM gives 0). The foundation's guard looked only at the method's own class.

The second is a final static whose initializer, run by the lemma's proof in the harness's state, reads what a caller changes before it initializes the class: a static (setThenOwn), the default locale (turkishThenLowered) and another class's array (setThenCopied).

The third is a StringBuilder a final static holds, read by the model directly or through a method reference (appendThenLogged and appendThenLoggedThroughLambda). The model's reads never asked Engine::reads.

Summaries are no stream's this run, so they are refused here (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs, strings.rs). No summary is used while any class is being initialized; the call runs as written, so seen and heldSeen are now violations, as on a JVM. Class initializers a lemma's proof runs are held to the lemma's read gate, and objects there when one starts or returns count as there before the call. A lemma reads no StringBuilder that was there before the call.

Tried and found guarded, each with its guard named in the README: a lambda's captured array, the ArrayList model, reflection, self-recursive and mutual lemmas, Pattern and Matcher, model statics, and an induction measure.

### A pair of versions' two runs of one loop past the bound go on from one state where they run the same code from the same state

change `owrsowqmmtyo` · [log `b436d23dc550`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/f28025bc-e46b-4a87-a943-bfb79dea5465/b436d23dc5500d8df0f8ce9da820c55a060649ad0a2ee1fb09aaca95ba6e32ea.jsonl.gz)

Example 287's preservation stopped at a counterexample no run has: past bcrypt's loops each side's state was free bits of its own, so two runs equal in fact were two states in the formula. The tool's own checker now names those bits by the state the loop is summarized from (lib/src/bmc/ties.rs, wired into bmc/loops.rs and bmc/mod.rs, with shared::fingerprint comparing the code). A summary of the same code from the same state, on either side, takes the same bits, and a read past such a loop at an index the path does not follow is named by the array's content and the index. The key is everything an iteration can read: the code with everything it reaches, the head, the live locals, the objects reachable from them and from the static fields that code uses (numbered as reached, so an alias is part of it), the JDK's statics and the classes' initialization. Only values are shared; each side leaves the loop by its own code. This is step 2's boundary, chosen over the unchanged callee as one function (which would have to carry crypt_raw's effects across heaps) and a coupled invariant; the brief's Progress says why.

Countermodels first (lib/tests/pairing.rs, seven variants of one table-mixing loop): a callee changed inside the loop, a cell, an alias on one side, a mutable static, a shorter array and a write past the loop on one side each differ on a JVM and are not proved, and five of them were Verified with their side condition taken out (checked by hand with a switch since removed). The variant with no difference, 'cannot be verified' before, is proved in 0.5 s. A capped probe of 287 at bound 80: the new release's summaries of ekskey and crypt_raw take the previous release's bits and the spurious counterexample is gone; the check then reaches the key schedule and stops at the 240 s limit, mostly in crypt_raw's rounds loop's invariant search (287's notes). test_costs.py run --changed passes; validate_example.py 287 passes.

- `String.valueOf` is modelled when its argument is a String or null. For any other object it is still a gap, and the gap scan still lists it.
